title: Inverse-tube width of a near-convergent word empties for a reason that is not an archived floor cell
statement: For every sufficiently balanced finance-admissible O/E word W, the exact inverse tube of W contracts below integer occupancy before |W| for a reason that is not empty_ooe / empty_oe / empty_odd_cell / ooe_cell / 243<256, and that contraction is detected by real or exponent hull width.
counterexamples: 9 --OOE--> 11 occupies a real hull of width 0.221 < 1
Beatty packed, bunched (OOE)^6, OE-front, interleave, and extra-odd prefixes all die at empty_ooe / k=3 on y=1000001
Max R_W on packed/bunched prefixes is 7 at both 10^2 and 10^6; no log-scale growth in the window
notes: Phase 0 only. Width is a hull relaxation of the archived OOE cell. No K=11, no 1054k, no L=55293, no floor raise. No Paper A edit, no ledger row, no Lean. Not a halt theorem.
tested_range: Complete end-E prefixes of length <= 18; inverse y in {11,101,1001,10001,100001,1000001}; forward 80 odds at 10^2..10^6; calibration {365,11681,14237,15343,27623,1000057}
